issue_context.title: Webhook doesn't get triggered on Image push
issue_context.body:
### Description

Whenever I push a new docker image to the package registry of my repository, the specified webhook doesn't get triggered.
I checked the "Package" checkbox in the custom events section and the image is indeed getting pushed to the registry when I watch the timestamp.
What I also noticed is, when I try to test the delivery with only "Package" checked, the test button does nothing. But when I change the radius input to either "All events" or "Push Events" the test button works fine and the history shows successful deliveries.

Is this a missconfiguration on my side or maybe a bug?
I want to trigger a GitOps Webhook after the image has been pushed to the registry so I guessed this is the right way.

### Gitea Version

1.18.3

### Can you reproduce the bug on the Gitea demo site?

Yes

review_comments: I don't quite like using `db.DefaultContext` in `routers`, but I'll allow it for now.
The notification should not use a transaction context. That's the reason why I use the `DefaultContext`.
If the `pv/pd` is created inside an uncommited transaction, then does `GetPackageDescriptor(db.DefaultContext, pv)` work? I haven't read the code, just a question.

Yes, the only "problem" is if satelite data (the owner/creator, repository, ...) referenced by that package version is deleted between the commit and the `GetPackageDescriptor` call. But in that case `GetPackageDescriptor` just returns an error.

Hmm, I am not sure about what the "yes" means ....

* If the "yes" means that: it works, because there is no uncommited transaction when calling notifyPackageCreate, then no problem.
* If the "yes" means that: `GetPackageDescriptor(db.DefaultContext, pv)` could read uncommited data, then I do not think so. Uncommited transaction data couldn't be read by other transactions.

Maybe the stable logic could be: `GetPackageDescriptor(dbCtx)` and `NotifyPackageCreate(DefaultContext)`, then there won't be problem.
"Yes" as "there is no uncommitted transaction". A lot of the notify methods collect their data inside the method. In this case the data-collections happens before the notification.

For sqlite3, if a transaction hasn't been committed or rollback, starting another transaction in the same go routine will result in a deadlock. I'm OK here because I don't think a notification failure should rollback the previous work. notification should be failure allowed.
I have read code   after the question. The  notifyPackageCreate is called after the transaction commit. So no problem
